projects.title: X-SPUR: Explainable Unsupervised IDS for Automotive Ethernet 📄
projects.bodyText: First-author paper published in *IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics* (Q1, JIF 9.8).
projects.detailBody:
📄 **Published in IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics (TII)**: Q1, top 6.8% in Automation & Control Systems (JCR), JIF 9.8

**X-SPUR: Explainable Surprisal-Based Protocol-Aware Unsupervised Reasoning for Automotive Ethernet Intrusion Detection**

An explainable, unsupervised intrusion detection framework for automotive Ethernet networks. Instead of relying on labeled attack data or handcrafted features, X-SPUR represents raw packet fields as token sequences, learns normal network behavior from benign traffic through causal language modeling, and detects anomalies from token-level surprisal. It also provides intrinsic, field-level explanations of anomalous traffic, showing analysts not only *whether* something is unusual but also *where* the anomaly originates.

First-author work conducted at SNSec Lab, Sookmyung Women's University, advised by Prof. Seonghoon Jeong.

projects.title: HEART: Harm Estimation and Ranking of Traffic for Cache-Hit-Ratio Recovery in E-Commerce Logs
projects.bodyText: BOAZ ADV-project on ranking e-commerce sessions by the cache harm they cause. Accepted as a regular paper at *IEEE BigData 2026* (acceptance rate 19.4%).
projects.detailBody:
📄 **Accepted as a regular paper at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData 2026)**, acceptance rate 19.4% (203 of 1,046 submissions)

**Beyond Bot Labels: Retrospective Consequence-Grounded Ranking of Attributed Cache Harm in E-Commerce Logs**

A BOAZ advanced project on cache pollution in e-commerce web logs. Instead of classifying which sessions are bots, it ranks sessions by the cache harm they actually cause: a single chronological cache replay charges each shopper's eviction-induced miss to the session that evicted the object, and a behavioral model learns to predict that harm without User-Agent labels. On a 12.7M-request real trace, the top 1% of sessions carry 48.8% of the harm, about half of it from sessions without bot tags. Bypassing the top-ranked sessions recovers 93% of a User-Agent baseline's cache-hit-ratio gain while selecting 47× fewer sessions.

With Youngwoo Seo (Korea University), advised by Prof. Seonghoon Jeong.
